newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight orders ease, charterers await fixing.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight orders ease, charterers await fixing.

text.p: London's sugar freight market was more subdued on Tuesday with few orders cited after the spate of fresh inquiry at the start of the week, shipbrokers said.

Vitol was in the market for 12/14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to the Black Sea for 2/5 December. Shipbrokers said the only Cuban order currently floated in the market, issued by Nissho Iwai earlier this month, remained to be filled. Seven Seas quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to a range of options for 22/28 November -- Mediterranean, Black Sea, Red Sea, east Africa, Pakistan, Colombo and Bangladesh.

Elsewhere, physical sugar traders said Polish white sugar was likely to be delivered against the expiry of London's December futures contract, as two major trade houses had a already issued freight orders specifying Polish ports.
